To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ni accumulation ability of rice cultivars is mainly affected by the varieties, and that the Ni accumulation in rice grains is closely associated with the soil Ni content.

The Ni concentrations of different Indica rice cultivar grains were in the range of 0.04-1.82 mg kg(-1) and the transfer factors (soil-to-grain) of different Indica cultivars were in the range from 0.04 to 1.82, with a mean of about 0.5, which were significantly lower than those of Japonica rice.
the Ni accumulation ability in different rice cultivars was significantly different and that the difference was mainly attributed to varieties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accumulation of Ni in rice grains, and the results will be helpful for the planning of rice cultivation in Ni-polluting areas.
the accumulation of soil Ni in the grains of different Indica rice cultivar.
the accumulation of Ni by rice in Ni-polylluted soils and the difference in the accumulation ability of various Indicarice cultivars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ni accumulation ability of the Indica rice cultivar was in the order of two-line hybrid rice > three-line hybrid rice>conventional rice.
the rice varieties with low soil-to-grain Ni transfer factors were the best cultivars for cultivation on Ni-polluted paddy soils.
the Ni accumulation ability of rice is closely associated with the varieties of rice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soil Ni concentration of 0.2 mg/kg is a critical value for the accumulation of Ni in rice.
the Ni accumulation ability of Indica rice cultivar is related to the cultivar, the soil Ni and the available soil Ni.

the rice cultivars with high Ni accumulation ability should be avoided to grow in the soils with available Ni higher than 0.1mg/kg, while the cultivars with low Ni accumulation ability could be used to grow in the soil with available Ni higher or lower than 0. 1mg/kg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ni accumulation of rice grains is mainly affected by soil Ni and the variety, and the soil-to-grain Ni transfer factors of rice cultivars can be calculated by using regression method.
Ni concentration in rice grains was positively correlated with the available soil Ni.
the soil-to-grain trans-fer factor is a more reliable parameter than the grain concentration for assessing Ni accumulation in rice.
